title: End-to-end SLO shadowing and failover rehearsal canvas
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary: Build an end-to-end SLO shadowing pipeline and a failover rehearsal canvas that lets us mirror SLI calculations (token-level latency, p95/p99, error rates) into a shadow SLO environment and run controlled regional failovers without impacting production traffic. The goal is to detect SLO drift before customers are impacted and to validate circuit-breaker + load-shedding behavior in a repeatable dashboard-driven workflow.

Background: We frequently see subtle regressions in tail latency after kernel/quantization changes and region capacity shifts. Existing dashboards show live SLOs but we lack a reliable mechanism to compute SLOs on mirrored traffic (shadow SLOs) and to exercise the multi-region failover decision path end-to-end. Shadowing will compute SLIs in parallel and tag divergence events. The rehearsal canvas will orchestrate progressive traffic redirections to validate fallback policies and circuit breaker engagement.

Goals:
- Implement a shadow SLI pipeline that computes token-level latency SLIs (p50/p95/p99), token admit rate, and error-rate per-tenant using mirrored traffic streams.
- Surface a Grafana canvas with panels for SLO divergence, shadow vs live diff, per-sequence-length cohorts, and model-variant regressions.
- Create a failover rehearsal runbook that executes staged region failovers (canary, partial, full) against the shadow SLOs first and records outcomes.
- Add automated alerts when divergence exceeds thresholds for >5 minutes and attach remediation steps.

Non-goals:
- Not implementing global traffic routing changes in production during initial rollout. Rehearsals will start on mirrored/staged clusters.
- Not replacing existing SLO derivation logic; shadow pipeline should re-use current SLI definitions where possible.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Shadow SLI pipeline runs for 72h on mirrored traffic and produces metrics with <5% sampling loss.
- Grafana canvas contains panels for: shadow vs live SLO delta, token-level p99 heatmap by sequence length, admit-rate waterfall, error-mode breakdown, and rehearsal timeline.
- Rehearsal runbook can be executed by SRE on staging with documented play-by-play and automated rollback.
- Alerts trigger when shadow-live p95 delta > 30ms or shadow p99 exceeds live p99 by >10%.

Design / Implementation notes:
- Mirror path: ingress proxy will fork a sampled subset (configurable sample rate default 5%) to the shadow SLI pipeline. Mirror traffic is stripped of customer-identifying payloads and routed to an SLI-collector cluster.
- SLI computation: compute token-latency at decode-step granularity and aggregate into sequence-level p50/p95/p99. Store aggregates in the metrics DB (time-series) with a shadow tag (env=shadow).
- Cohorting: group by sequence length bins (0-64,65-256,257-1024), model variant, and region.
- Failover rehearsal: use staged routing rules to shift a small percentage of production traffic on a test cohort to alternate region/model pools while keeping live production flow unchanged. The rehearsal engine writes events to rehearsal-log for correlation with shadow metrics.
- Circuit-breaker validation: simulate admission pressure to verify circuit opens according to configured thresholds and that load-shedding policies reduce admit rates gracefully.

Telemetry queries (examples):
- Shadow vs live p99 diff (PromQL): sum by (region,model,seq_bin) (histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket{env!="shadow"}[5m]))) - sum by (region,model,seq_bin) (histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket{env=="shadow"}[5m])))
- Admit rate waterfall (SQL/time-series): SELECT time_bucket('1m', ts) as minute, region, model, seq_bin, sum(admitted_tokens)/sum(requested_tokens) as admit_rate FROM token_metrics WHERE env='shadow' OR env='prod' GROUP BY minute, region, model, seq_bin

Dashboard panels to build:
- Shadow vs Live SLO Delta: time-series with annotations for rehearsals and deploys.
- Token p99 Heatmap: matrix of p99 by seq_bin and model variant (shadow and live side-by-side).
- Admit Rate Waterfall: stacked bar showing per-tenant admit vs reject across regions.
- Error-mode Breakdown: pie/table of decode failures, OOMs, timeouts.
- Rehearsal Timeline: events list and scatter showing when circuit-breakers opened and how traffic shifted.

Rollout plan:
1) Dev: implement SLI collector and histogram ingestion on dev cluster with synthetic traffic.
2) Staging: enable mirrored sampling from staging ingress at 5% for 72h. Build Grafana canvas and verify queries.
3) Shadow run: enable mirrored production sampling at 1% for a week and evaluate divergence.
4) Rehearsal: run staged failover rehearsals on shadow pipeline and document outcomes.
5) Gradual ramp: increase sampling and automate alerts.

Risks and mitigations:
- Cost: mirror traffic increases metrics volume — mitigate by sampling and histogram bucketing.
- Privacy: ensure payload scrubbing and tenant hashing before storing.
- False positives: calibrate divergence thresholds per cohort to avoid noisy alerts.

Open decisions:
- Whether to compute token-latency histograms client-side (proxy) vs server-side collector. Server-side simplifies instrumentation but may miss client-side serialization costs.
- Sampling rate for production shadowing (1% vs 5%).
